messages:
sanam: kicking off the quant sweep notes — focused on open-13b-v2 variants (int4 vs int8) + a 7b baseline. goal = sweetspot for product routing (cost vs quality).

mike: quick bench numbers from the cluster run earlier today. p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec for 512 context:
- 13b-int4: p50 95ms, p95 260ms, 180 tok/s
- 13b-int8: p50 130ms, p95 360ms, 120 tok/s
- 7b-int4: p50 55ms, p95 170ms, 320 tok/s

ravi: can you paste the unit cost calc? need to show PM.

mike: sure — rough econ from cluster billing + perf:```
# cost per 1M output tokens (approx)
13b-int4: $340
13b-int8: $620
7b-int4: $115
```
numbers include GPU time, infra overhead, and amortized model storage.

leah: quality quick-check from eval harness (100 prompt probe set focused on retrieval QA + instruction following):
- 13b-int8: 87% pass rate (strict), mean hallucination score 0.06
- 13b-int4: 82% pass rate, mean hallucination score 0.09 (edge regressions on factuality)
- 7b-int4: 71% pass rate, hallucination 0.18

sanam: good, so int4 for 13b has small quality delta vs int8 but ~45% cost savings. product asks: recommend single-model route or hybrid?

ravi: hybrid looks promising: route high-SLA flows (billing, legal text, finance) to 13b-int8; low-risk short prompts to 7b-int4 or 13b-int4. fallback policy if quality check fails.

leah: added thresholding idea — do cheap quick pass on 7b-int4, then re-score risky outputs with 13b-int8 only if confidence < 0.6. reduces RPS to heavy model.

mike: quick pseudo of routing rule we tested:```json
{
  "route": [
    {"predicate": "task in ['billing','contract']", "model": "13b-int8"},
    {"predicate": "confidence < 0.6", "model": "13b-int8", "fallback": "sync"},
    {"predicate": "else", "model": "7b-int4"}
  ]
}
```
ran a sim with real traffic sample — cost down 42% vs always-13b-int8, quality loss <1.5% on measured metrics.

sanam: any regressions of note for int4 13b? specific categories?

leah: yes, two main buckets:
1) long-context synthesis where rare facts get truncated (int4 tends to be slightly less stable on very long inputs).
2) numeric reasoning — occasional off-by-one. both are small but visible on legal/finance prompts.

ravi: ops question — does int4 require different KV cache memory tuning? we saw some OOM-ish logs on 1 GPU jobs.

mike: int4 reduces model weights but increases marginal CPU work for dequantization in our runtime; default cache windows needed to be reduced from 2048->1536 for stable runs on 80GB A100. noted in the deploy logs. deploy-bot posted the infra alert earlier.

deploy-bot: [alert] 13b-int4 shard-3 hit memory pressure on 2026-03-15T09:12:22Z, auto-scale triggered +1 replica.

sanam: ops action: add profile to Dedicated autoscale policy to pre-warm +1 replica when quant job scheduled. also update docs on recommended cache window.

leah: product recommendation draft for GTN:
- Default: hybrid routing (7b-int4 for low-value flows, 13b-int4 for mid, 13b-int8 for high-value/SLAs)
- Safety: always re-score high-risk outputs with 13b-int8 based on confidence heuristics
- Observability: expose token-level cost in Console and per-route quality deltas; auto-alert if regression >2% on eval bouquet

ravi: +1. also suggest an A/B runway: start with 10% traffic on hybrid vs baseline for 2 weeks, track cost delta and P99 latency, QA pass rate.

mike: one more - pruning the prompt engineering helps: short templates + early truncation reduced int4 hallucinations by ~0.8% in our probe. worth adding to playbook.

sanam: thanks all. next steps: mike to drop perf & infra notes into the onboarding doc; leah to produce the GTN-facing one-pager; ravi to owner A/B and rollout. I'll file the canary run for next Tue. :thumbsup:

leah: uploading eval artifacts to the bundle now — will share link when ready.

eval-bot: artifact bundle uploaded: s3://redwood-eval/1955557777/13b-quant-sweep/v1 (contains probe results, logs, and cost sims).
